newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: US trade rep seeks Asia support on telecoms, tech.
newsitem.headline: US trade rep seeks Asia support on telecoms, tech.

text.p: Deputy U.S. Trade Representative Jeffrey Lang said on Thursday the U.S. is seeking Asia's commitment for proposals to liberalise telecommunication services and reduce tariffs on technology products.

On an official visit to Malaysia, where he met with government officials, Lang said: "I think we can now see the possibility ahead of an information technology agreement which would eliminate tariffs by the year 2000 on all the goods that go into the global information infrastructure."

Lang, who was just in Singapore and is going on to Jakarta, Bangkok and New Delhi, also told reporters there were signs a deal could be reached on a new telecommunications services pact that would "help to lower everybody's phone bill in the world."

"These deals cannot be successful without commitments from Asia," Lang said, adding that he was talking with his counterparts in the region prior to the World Trade Organisation (WTO) trade ministers' conference in Singapore in December.

The WTO telecommunications talks aim to set a timetable to liberalise telecommunication services, investment policies and regulations to promote greater interconnectivity and international competition.
The move to remove tariffs on information technology is supported by the Asia Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) forum of which the U.S. is a member.
If successful, the tariff removals would lower the cost of everything from computers to mobile phones across the 18 APEC members.
